newsitem.title: USA: CBO data may show $185-200 bln 2002 US deficit-Sen.
newsitem.headline: CBO data may show $185-200 bln 2002 US deficit-Sen.

text.p: Sen. Pete Domenici, chairman of the Senate Budget Committee, said on Sunday Congressional Budget Office (CBO) figures would show a fiscal year 2002 federal budget deficit of $185 billion to $200 billion.

"I believe that the Congressional Budget Office estimates will show this deficit is going back up," Domenici told CNN's Late Edition program. "In the sixth year, the year we want to balance, I think it will be between $185 and $200 billion."

Domenici, a New Mexico Republican, said that the CBO has been instructed to give its economic assumptions to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), which drafts the White House budget, as soon as it has prepared them.
The administration of President Bill Clinton, a Democrat, is seeking to produce a budget that would balance the federal budget by 2002 under its own economic assumptions or those of the CBO.
The CBO operates under the aegis of the Congress, both of whose houses are now controlled by Republicans.
Last week, a White House official said the administration expected to get CBO's economic assumptions on Monday Dec. 9.
But the official said the critical "technical" assumptions laying out expected tax revenues, government expenditures and the resulting deficit, were not expected until later.

Earlier, OMB Director Franklin Raines said on the same CNN program that the White House would need the CBO figures by Christmas in order to produce a budget proposal that would balance the budget under either set of assumptions.
